\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{پرورش} \ur{کرنا} (parvarish karnā)}{پرورش کرنا (parvarish karnā)}]{\ur{پرورش} \ur{کرنا} (parvarish karnā) — to raise a child; to bring up}

\label{lesson:UR-C484-parvarish-karna}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for birth, then the Urdu for a newborn.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{پرورش} \ur{کرنا}}
\textbf{\ur{پرورش} \ur{کرنا}} — \emph{parvarish karnā} — \textquotedblleft{}to raise a child; to bring up\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{نانی} \ur{نے} \ur{میری} \ur{پرورش} \ur{کی۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{nānī ne merī parvarish kī.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
My grandmother brought me up.
\end{quote}

Past, with \ur{نے} (he or she …): \ur{اس} \ur{نے} \ur{بیٹی} \ur{کی} \ur{پرورش} \ur{کی}, \emph{us ne beṭī kī parvarish kī}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{پرورش} \ur{کرنا}} (\emph{parvarish karnā}) is built from \textbf{\ur{پرورش}}, usually traced to Persian \emph{parvarish}, \textquotedblleft{}nurture\textquotedblright{}, and \textbf{\ur{کرنا}}, \textquotedblleft{}to do\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{parvarish karnā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{parvarish karnā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{nānī ne merī parvarish kī.} — My grandmother brought me up.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for birth, then the Urdu for a newborn, then say \emph{parvarish karnā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ur{پرورش} \ur{کرنا} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To raise a child; to bring up\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{لوری} (lorī)}{لوری (lorī)}]{\ur{لوری} (lorī) — a lullaby}

\label{lesson:UR-C484-lori}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for a newborn, then the Urdu for to raise a child.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{لوری}}
\textbf{\ur{لوری}} — \emph{lorī} — \textquotedblleft{}a lullaby\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{ماں} \ur{رات} \ur{کو} \ur{لوری} \ur{گاتی} \ur{ہے۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{māṅ rāt ko lorī gātī hai.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The mother sings a lullaby at night.
\end{quote}

Feminine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{لوری}} (\emph{lorī}) is inherited: CDIAL lists the Hindi cousin \emph{lorī} under \emph{lōḍa}, \textquotedblleft{}tossing, swinging\textquotedblright{}, a form it reconstructs (CDIAL 11136): the song of the rocking cradle.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{lorī}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{lorī}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{māṅ rāt ko lorī gātī hai.} — The mother sings a lullaby at night.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for a newborn, then the Urdu for to raise a child, then say \emph{lorī} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ur{لوری} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A lullaby\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{جھلانا} (jhulānā)}{جھلانا (jhulānā)}]{\ur{جھلانا} (jhulānā) — to rock; to swing (someone)}

\label{lesson:UR-C484-jhulana}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for to raise a child, then the Urdu for a lullaby.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{جھلانا}}
\textbf{\ur{جھلانا}} — \emph{jhulānā} — \textquotedblleft{}to rock; to swing (someone)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{دادی} \ur{بچے} \ur{کو} \ur{جھلا} \ur{رہی} \ur{تھیں۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{dādī bachche ko jhulā rahī thīṅ.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
My grandmother was rocking the baby.
\end{quote}

Past, with \ur{نے} (he or she …): \ur{اس} \ur{نے} \ur{بچے} \ur{کو} \ur{جھلایا}, \emph{us ne bachche ko jhulāyā}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{جھلانا}} (\emph{jhulānā}) is the causative of \emph{jhūlnā}, \textquotedblleft{}to swing\textquotedblright{}, which CDIAL lists under \emph{jhulyati}, \textquotedblleft{}swings\textquotedblright{}, a form it reconstructs (CDIAL 5406).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{jhulānā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{jhulānā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{dādī bachche ko jhulā rahī thīṅ.} — My grandmother was rocking the baby.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for to raise a child, then the Urdu for a lullaby, then say \emph{jhulānā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ur{جھلانا} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To rock; to swing (someone)\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{کھلانا} (khilānā)}{کھلانا (khilānā)}]{\ur{کھلانا} (khilānā) — to feed}

\label{lesson:UR-C484-khilana}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for a lullaby, then the Urdu for to rock.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{کھلانا}}
\textbf{\ur{کھلانا}} — \emph{khilānā} — \textquotedblleft{}to feed\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{ماں} \ur{بچے} \ur{کو} \ur{کھانا} \ur{کھلاتی} \ur{ہے۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{māṅ bachche ko khānā khilātī hai.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The mother feeds the child.
\end{quote}

Past, with \ur{نے} (he or she …): \ur{اس} \ur{نے} \ur{بچے} \ur{کو} \ur{کھانا} \ur{کھلایا}, \emph{us ne bachche ko khānā khilāyā}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{کھلانا}} (\emph{khilānā}) is the causative of \textbf{\ur{کھانا}}, \textquotedblleft{}to eat\textquotedblright{}, inherited from Sanskrit \emph{khādati}, \textquotedblleft{}chews, eats\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 3865).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{پلانا} (pilānā)}{پلانا (pilānā)}]{\ur{پلانا} (pilānā) — to give (someone) a drink}

\label{lesson:UR-C484-pilana}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for to rock, then the Urdu for to feed.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{پلانا}}
\textbf{\ur{پلانا}} — \emph{pilānā} — \textquotedblleft{}to give (someone) a drink\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{نرس} \ur{نے} \ur{مریض} \ur{کو} \ur{پانی} \ur{پلایا۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{nars ne marīz ko pānī pilāyā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The nurse gave the patient some water to drink.
\end{quote}

Past, with \ur{نے} (he or she …): \ur{اس} \ur{نے} \ur{بچے} \ur{کو} \ur{دودھ} \ur{پلایا}, \emph{us ne bachche ko dūdh pilāyā}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{پلانا}} (\emph{pilānā}) is the causative of \textbf{\ur{پینا}}, \textquotedblleft{}to drink\textquotedblright{}, inherited from Sanskrit \emph{píbati}, \textquotedblleft{}drinks\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 8209).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for to rock, then the Urdu for to feed, then say \emph{pilānā} again
